title: manifest fields advertise a subset of the record keys (task list and task view)
description: Surfaced by QCLI-312/QCLI-291 while building --fields under DEC-161. The accept-set for --fields is the fields quest manifest --json advertises for the command (ruling A), and for BOTH task list and task view that advertised set is a curated subset of the top-level keys the records carry. Measured: task list items carry more keys than the 13 advertised; task view records carry more than the 29 advertised, including blockers, gates and gateEvents, so task view --fields blockers (etc.) is refused as an unknown field. Also noted by the QCLI-291 review. The pre-existing contract test asserts only declared subset-of payload, never payload subset-of declared, so nothing catches the understatement. Not DEC-161 work and not started there.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Quest manifest --json advertises for task list every top-level key a task list item carries, and for task view every top-level key a task view record carries (payload is a subset of declared), asserted in that direction by a test, not only declared-subset-of-payload
The help or the manifest states unambiguously what a command fields array means when the payload varies by record (a curated subset vs a complete key set), so a consumer can tell which it is reading

plan: Determine the COMPLETE top-level key set for a task list item and a task view record from the emitting code, not a sample
Set the manifest fields for task list and task view to those complete sets
Add a test asserting payload is a SUBSET of declared (every emitted key is declared) for both commands, in that direction
State unambiguously in the help/manifest what a fields array means (AC2), so a consumer can tell complete-set from curated-subset
run bun run check, review, land
implementationNotes:
QCLI-461 implementation.

FIELDS ARE NOW THE COMPLETE KEY SET. For the read surfaces, `fields` is the complete top-level key set a payload can carry, not a curated subset:
  task list  = the task record keys + path
  task view  = the task record keys + path + revision + the conditional notesOmitted
  search     = the task record keys (search adds no path)
The record key set is enumerated from the TaskState interface, so a key appears in a payload only when that record carries it, and the declared set is the union over records.

AC1's direction is asserted in test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts: payload-subset-of-declared (every key a payload carries is declared). That REPLACES the former declared-subset-of-payload assertion, which a curated subset satisfies while the record carries more -- the reason the manifest under-declared both records. The mirrored sets were updated together in test/contract/command-contract.test.ts, src/contract/tracker/fixtures.ts (the public conformance fixture) and src/contract/tracker/index.ts (the adapter probe required set, which fails closed on drift).

AC2: the manifest help and the task list / task view help now state the meaning -- `fields` is the COMPLETE key set a read command's `data` can carry (NOT a curated subset) and is exactly what --fields accepts; the settable-INPUT vocabulary of task create / task edit / task edit-batch is named as the exception so a consumer can tell which it is reading. A visible consequence: `task view --fields blockers` is now accepted, where the filing recorded it as refused.

SCOPE NOTE: the task names task list and task view. search carries the same defect and the same assertion covers it, so it was completed too rather than left under-declared beside a passing test. This is the same defect class on a third surface, not a new one.
